## Functional Specification

Domain: emulator
Summary: A CHIP-8 emulator that accurately executes CHIP-8 ROMs with proper timing, graphics, sound, and input handling

### Requirements (MUST implement)
- Must implement all 35 CHIP-8 opcodes with cycle-accurate behavior
- Must support 64x32 monochrome display with sprite drawing
- Must implement 16-key hexadecimal keypad input
- Must generate 60Hz buzzer sound when sound timer > 0
- Must execute at 500-1000 Hz CPU speed with configurable speed
- Must support ROM files up to 3584 bytes (0xE00 - 0x200)
- Must implement proper CHIP-8 memory layout with interpreter at 0x000-0x1FF
- Must handle 16-level stack for subroutine calls
- Must implement random number generation for 0xCXNN opcode
- Must properly handle collision detection in sprite drawing

### Data Structures
- 4096 bytes RAM (0x000-0xFFF)
- 64x32 pixel framebuffer (1 bit per pixel)
- 16 8-bit registers V0-VF (V0-VB general purpose, VC-F special)
- 16-bit index register I
- 16-bit program counter PC
- 8-bit delay timer
- 8-bit sound timer
- 16-level stack array of 16-bit values
- 8-bit stack pointer (0-15)
- 16-key keypad state array (true/false per key)

### Components
- **cpu** (complex, ~400 LOC)
  - fetch(): read 2 bytes big-endian from PC via memory.readWord()
  - decode(opcode): extract X, Y, N, NN, NNN fields
  - execute(opcode): switch on opcode pattern
  - execute0NNN(): execute machine language subroutine (NOP)
  - execute00E0(): clear screen via display.clear()
  - execute00EE(): return from subroutine via stack.pop()
  - execute1NNN(): jump to address NNN
  - execute2NNN(): call subroutine at NNN via stack.push(PC)
  - execute3XNN(): skip next if VX == NN
  - execute4XNN(): skip next if VX != NN
  - REQ: Fetch-decode-execute cycle at 500-1000 Hz
  - REQ: Implement all 35 CHIP-8 opcodes with accurate behavior
  - REQ: Handle timer decrement at 60Hz
  - REQ: Block on input opcodes until key pressed
  - REQ: Proper stack operations for calls/returns
- **memory** (simple, ~50 LOC)
  - read(address): return byte at address
  - write(address, value): store byte at address
  - readWord(address): return 2 bytes big-endian
  - writeWord(address, value): store 2 bytes big-endian
  - loadRom(data: Uint8Array): copy to 0x200
  - reset(): clear RAM, load fonts
  - loadFonts(): load 16 5-byte font sprites
  - REQ: Manage 4096 bytes of RAM
  - REQ: Load ROM at offset 0x200
  - REQ: Implement font sprites at 0x000-0x04F
  - REQ: Provide big-endian word read/write
- **display** (medium, ~100 LOC)
  - drawSprite(x, y, spriteData, height): draw sprite, return collision
  - clear(): clear entire screen
  - getPixel(x, y): return pixel state
  - setPixel(x, y, state): set pixel state
  - refresh(): notify display updated
  - getWidth(): return 64
  - getHeight(): return 32
  - REQ: Manage 64x32 pixel framebuffer
  - REQ: Implement sprite drawing with XOR and collision
  - REQ: Provide screen refresh interface
  - REQ: Handle sprite wrapping
- **input** (simple, ~50 LOC)
  - isKeyPressed(key): return true if key pressed (0-15)
  - waitForKey(): block until any key pressed, return key
  - keyDown(key): mark key as pressed
  - keyUp(key): mark key as released
  - reset(): release all keys
  - REQ: Track state of 16 hexadecimal keys
  - REQ: Block until key pressed for FX0A
  - REQ: Provide key mapping from keyboard
- **sound** (simple, ~50 LOC)
  - play(): start 440Hz square wave
  - stop(): stop audio
  - setFrequency(hz): change tone frequency
  - isPlaying(): return playing state
  - REQ: Generate 60Hz square wave tone
  - REQ: Play when sound timer > 0
  - REQ: Stop when sound timer = 0
- **timer** (simple, ~30 LOC)
  - start(): begin 60Hz ticks
  - stop(): stop ticks
  - tick(): call cpu.updateTimers()
  - REQ: Generate 60Hz tick for timers
  - REQ: Call CPU timer update

### Integration Rules (CRITICAL)
- CPU owns registers, timers, stack, stack pointer, PC
- Memory owns RAM array, provides read/write interface
- Display owns framebuffer, provides draw/clear interface
- Input owns keypad state, provides isKeyPressed interface
- Sound owns audio context, provides play/stop interface
- Timer owns 60Hz tick, provides update interface
- cpu MUST use injected dependencies via their interfaces. Do NOT duplicate state that other modules own.
- timer MUST use injected dependencies via their interfaces. Do NOT duplicate state that other modules own.
- Each component owns its own state. Other components access it ONLY through the public interface — never copy internal data.
- Use camelCase for all method names. No snake_case.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Can load and execute IBM logo ROM displaying proper logo
- Can run CHIP-8 games like Pong, Space Invaders, Tetris
- All 35 opcodes pass test ROMs
- Sound plays correctly when programs use sound timer
- Input responds correctly to keypad presses
- Display shows proper graphics without flickering
- No memory leaks or crashes during extended gameplay
